subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A geologic period is a named interval of Earth's history.
• Sometimes, geologists officially replace an older period name with a new one.
• Geologists adopted "Tertiary" as an official period name in 1829.
• The Paleogene and Neogene replaced the Tertiary in 2004.
• The Paleogene and Neogene remain the officially recognized period names.
prompt: The student wants to specify how long geologists officially used the term "Tertiary." Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Geologists sometimes replace older period names with new ones, as they did when the Paleogene and Neogene replaced the Tertiary.
choices.B: Though the Paleogene and Neogene are currently used, the term they replaced was adopted in 1829.
choices.C: The term "Tertiary" was an official geologic period name from 1829 to 2004.
choices.D: The Paleogene and Neogene have been official period names since 2004, when they replaced the Tertiary.

explanation: Choice C is the best answer. The sentence directly specifies how long geologists officially used the term "Tertiary," stating that it was an official geologic period name from 1829 to 2004.
